snippet.title: How to actually survive as a CS major in 2026 #computerscience #tech #coding
snippet.description:
👇🏼 Is a computer science degree still worth it in 2026? 

Short answer: yes, but only if you stop treating it like a finish line.

Here’s the data everyone’s ignoring. A CS degree carries one of the highest ROIs of any major (~716%, per Research.com), and the Bureau of Labor Statistics projects computing jobs to grow 22% through 2033 which is far faster than average. Early-career CS grads earn ~$87K vs ~$58K for the average major (NY Fed).

So why does it feel like this right now? Because entry-level hiring got harder. Layoffs + a flood of new grads = real competition for that first job. The bar went up and it’s staying up.

The degree isn’t dead. The passive version of it is.
The grads winning in 2026 aren’t grinding LeetCode in silence , they’re building in public and learning to direct AI instead of competing with it. AI-augmented over afraid.

Save this if you’re about to pick your major. 📌

Building anything right now? Tell me below 👇

Sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (2024), NY Fed Labor Market for Recent Grads, Research.com (2026)
